newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister still mired in Pele row.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister still mired in Pele row.

text.p: Brazil's transport minister, denounced last week for a "racist" comment about national soccer legend Pele, agreed on Tuesday to lobby for black rights in parliament, Globo television said.
But despite profuse apologies, Eliseu Padilha failed to assuage representatives from 17 black rights groups at a two-hour meeting on Tuesday, and now faces criminal and civil actions over his remark.
Speaking at a transport seminar last Thursday, Padilha said: "There are two blacks admired in Brazil. One is Pele, forever our king. The other is King Asphalt; everybody likes asphalt."

When reporters questioned him about the statement, he said he did not mean to demean Pele and was merely repeating a comment he had heard elsewhere. Padilha later apologised to Pele and said the press had wrongly interpreted his remarks as being racist.
"The minister will have every opportunity to apologise in court," Ivanir dos Santos, executive secretary of the Centre for Expression of Marginalized Populations, told television.

"Various Brazilian blacks are explaining themselves in court. They form the majority (of inmates) in Brazilian jails, and nobody thinks that if they apologise, they will be absolved," dos Santos added.
Padilha will be prosecuted under a Brazilian law that makes racism a crime.

"My relationship with the movement and with the black citizens of Brazil at this moment is a question of ethics and of moral relation. The judicial question is a question we will judge at the appropriate moment," a shaken Padilha said on television.

Pele, whose name is Edson Arantes do Nascimento, is Brazil's sports minister. Although viewed abroad as one of the world's greatest athletes during his long soccer career, he has complained about being subjected to racism back home in Brazil.
But he dismissed Padilha's remark as clumsiness and said he did not take offence.
